name: Direct cinema and vérité
summary: A handheld 16mm camera and a synchronised tape recorder stay with real people. No script, no set and no lamps. The camera sits in the room and waits. The picture is rough, and the sound is complete.

philosophy.core_thesis: Light gear and sync sound let the camera watch people in real time, so the film is made of what happens and not of what is staged.
design_principles: Shoot with a handheld 16mm camera and a synchronised tape recorder, with a crew of 2 to 3 people.
Use the available light only, with a fast stock pushed 1 to 2 stops, and let a window blow out to white.
Frame in 1.33:1 or 1.37:1 at eye level, with a 10mm to 25mm zoom or a 9.5mm to 25mm lens, and let the subject move out of focus for 1 to 3 s.
Hold a take of 20 to 120 s and cut at an average shot length of 8 to 15 s, with no cutaway to hide a seam.
Never stage or ask for a repeat; follow the event at 1 to 1.5 m/s and arrive after it begins.
Record the real sound of the room and let people talk over each other; leave the voice-over out or limit it to 5% of the runtime.
Interview in the street or at home, and keep the question and the interviewer's voice in the cut.
anti_patterns: A voice-of-God narration over every shot
Studio lighting with a key and a fill
A tripod and a polished dolly move
A score laid over the events
A tidy interview in a set
A cutaway that hides a jump

composition.framing: A loose, shifting 1.33:1 frame; heads touch the edge, a back blocks the view, and the camera re-frames in the take.
composition.staging_in_depth: Whatever the room gives: 2 to 4 planes of people, with a foreground shoulder or a door that cuts the frame.
composition.subject_placement: Wherever the person is; the frame follows by 0.3 to 0.8 s late and then corrects.

principles.rule: Shoot a loose 1.33:1 frame at eye level and let a head or a shoulder cut the frame.
Follow the person who speaks or acts, and let the frame find them a little late.
Work in the room as it is: a foreground shoulder, the speaker and a window behind.
Use only the light in the room or the street, with no added lamp.
principles.value: 0 added lamps, 2:1 or less key to fill

principles.rule: Hold the take until the exchange ends, and cut at the end of an action.
principles.value: 8 to 15 s average shot, takes of 20 to 120 s

camera_and_movement.movement: A handheld follow with a pan and a zoom to find a face; the camera stays close, re-frames and breathes with the person.
camera_and_movement.support: Shoulder-mounted 16mm camera, handheld; a car or a chair for a ride
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Walking pace 1.0 to 1.5 m/s; a zoom over 1 to 3 s

lens_and_format.focal_length: 9.5mm to 25mm (16mm format), equal to about 20mm to 60mm in 35mm format; zoom 12mm to 120mm
lens_and_format.aperture: f/1.9 to f/4 with a fast stock pushed by 1 to 2 stops
lens_and_format.focus: A hand-held focus that drifts; the subject can go soft for 1 to 3 s.
equipment: fast 16mm stock pushed by 1 to 2 stops

light.quality: Whatever the place gives: window light, a bare bulb and street lamps, with deep shadows and burned highlights.
light.direction: From the window or a lamp in the frame; no key and no fill.
light.colour_temperature: Daylight 5600K or tungsten 3200K, left as found
light.source: Windows, bare bulbs and street lamps

colour_and_grade.treatment: Black and white with a rough, grainy full grey scale, or a plain colour print with no grade; the print shows its stock.
grade_recipe: Convert to black and white and set the black point at 5% and the white point at 97%.
Keep a plain contrast curve of +10% and let the windows clip.
Add grain at 25% to 35% to match 16mm stock pushed 2 stops.
Add 0.5% to 1% of frame jitter and a flash frame at the cut of a roll.
Do not add a tint, a LUT or a vignette.
colour_and_grade.texture: Coarse 16mm grain at 25% to 35%, with frame weave and flash frames

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 8 to 15 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 1 s for a cutaway of a face to 120 s for a long take
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut at the end of an action or a line, and keep the take as it ran, so the viewer sees a real event. Keep the jump when the camera runs out of film.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut, a flash frame at a roll change, a short black of 1 s and no dissolve.

sound.approach: Synchronous location sound, with a boom or a lavalier; all noise of the place stays in the track.
sound.dialogue: Unrehearsed and overlapping; the interviewer's question stays in the track and subtitles are used for translation only.
sound.music: Only the music that is in the room: a band, a radio or a song on stage; no score.
sound.loudness: −23 LUFS integrated for a restoration, with a wide dynamic range

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A plain title card in white on black or over the first shot; the date and the place in a lower-third caption.
titles_and_graphics.type: A plain sans-serif in white upper case, 2 to 4 s for the title, 1 to 2 s for a caption.

shot_primer.opening: Open in the middle of an event with sound already running; the first cut comes after 10 to 20 s.

positive: flash frame at a roll change

emotion.target_response: Presence and doubt: the viewer is in the room with real people and feels that nothing is arranged.

use_cases: video prompts for a real-event look
avoid_when: The brief needs a staged hero shot or a controlled colour.
The piece needs a narrator to explain a complex argument.

modifiers.how: Keep the location and the plain light; write the scene, cast non-professionals and move the camera on a slow dolly.
Keep the black and white; shorten the average shot to 2 to 3 s and join shots by contrast, not by the order of events.

sources.title: Stephen Mamber, Cinema Verite in America: Studies in Uncontrolled Documentary (MIT Press, 1974)
Erik Barnouw, Documentary: A History of the Non-Fiction Film (Oxford University Press, 2nd ed., 1993)
